deadlines.what_en: Last day to notify the tenant of any change to the lease terms, including the rent: at least 90 days before the lease ends on 31 Dec 2026 (Article 14). The tenant received the notice on 12 Oct 2026, 80 days before expiry, so the notice was late
End of the 15 days from the notice's date (24 Sep 2026) that the landlord gave the tenant to accept the increase and sign the renewal; it ended before the tenant received the notice on 12 Oct 2026
Vacate and hand over the warehouse when the lease ends, as the landlord demands if the increase is refused (contested by the claim)

claims.item_en: Declare the landlord's notice of 24 Sep 2026 without effect and renew the lease for one year at the same annual rent
In the alternative, set the fair annual rent for the renewal year at no more than this amount
Reject the landlord's demand that the tenant vacate on 31 Dec 2026

key_facts.fact_en: Annual rent AED 210,000; the landlord demands AED 252,000 at renewal, an increase of 20%

The notice is dated 24 Sep 2026, before the 90-day cut-off of 2 Oct 2026, but it was delivered by hand and the tenant received it only on 12 Oct 2026, 80 days before the lease ends; the receipt date is known only from the handwritten note
The average rent for similar units in the Dubai rent index is AED 240,000; the current rent is 12.5% below it, so under Article 1 of Decree No. 43 of 2013 the increase may not exceed 5% (AED 220,500)

The landlord threatens eviction at the end of the lease if the increase is refused; the claim answers that eviction at the end of a lease is allowed only on the Article 25(2) grounds, after 12 months' notice through the notary public or registered mail
The receipt note is signed by the tenant's receptionist (Reem) and stamped with the tenant's company stamp, which carries no date

citations.note_en: A real Dubai decree that is not in the official law library. Its Article 1 sets the maximum increase at renewal by how far the rent is below the average rent of similar units (5% when it is 11% to 20% below); checked on the Dubai Legislation Portal.

reader_should_flag: Dubai Decree No. 43 of 2013 on rent increases (Article 1) is a real decree that is not in the official law library, so the citation cannot be checked automatically and must be checked by hand.
The date the tenant received the landlord's notice, 12 Oct 2026, appears only in the handwritten receipt note on page 2; the claim does not print it.

The 90-day notice under Article 14 was not given: the lease ends on 31 Dec 2026, so notice was due by 2 Oct 2026 (computed). The notice is dated 24 Sep 2026, but the tenant received it on 12 Oct 2026, 80 days before expiry.
The 15 days the landlord gave to accept ran from the notice's date and ended on 9 Oct 2026 (computed), before the tenant received the notice.
The landlord demands a 20% increase (AED 252,000); with the rent 12.5% below the index average, Decree No. 43 of 2013 allows at most 5% (AED 220,500).
The eviction threat rests on none of the Article 25(2) grounds, and no 12-month notice through the notary public or registered mail was given.
